main_text.head: TETRASTICHON ORDINEM librorum N.T. exhibens.
main_text.p: Matthæus, Marcus, Lucas, Iohannes, & Acta. Roma: Corin: Galat: Ephes, Philip: Colosenses, Thessal: & Timotheus, Titus, Philemon, Hebr. Iacobi, Petri, Iohannis, & Iudas, Apoc. (raus[?]
main_text.head: NUMERUS CAPITUM SEU membrorum in libris N. T.
main_text.p: Matthæus septena quater, Marcusq; bis octo, Lucas sena quater: tot, tribus absq; Iohan. Actus dant septena quater, sed Roma bis octo, Prima, tot, urbs bimaris: posterior tredecim, Sex Galatis, Epheso totidem: sed deinde Philippis Quatuor, & totidem scripta Colossiacis. Thessalonica prius quinque, & tria postea coepit, Bis tria Timotheus, bis duo deinde simul, Sunt tria scripta Tito, Philemon legerat unum, Quinque Iacob, unum Iuda fidelis habet. Undecies binis Iohannes ultima scribit Tempore, sic sedus clauditur omne Novum.
main_text.head: IDEM MAIORIS PERSPICUITATIS gratia germanice.
main_text.p: Mattheus der hat viermal siben/ Marcus demnach sechzehen gschribe. In Luca vier vnd zwenzig sind/ In Johan dreyer minder sind. Die Gschichten acht vnd zwenzig hand Vnd Römer sind sechzehen gstandt. In eiden Brieffen gan Corinth Man sechzehen dreyzehen findt.

page.notes: The right edge of the scan shows part of the neighbouring page (a title and decorative initial); not transcribed. The page number at the top left is small and doubtful. The last word of the Tetrastich line ("(raus") is uncertain. The catchword "Sechs" is printed at the lower right in a ligatured form.
